Here’s the opportunity to stress that treatment should include biopsychosocial considerations. Discuss behavior management ideas for mother to use at home: identifying developmentally appropriate expectations, consistent consequences, rewarding appropriate behavior, etc.

Individual therapies (cognitively based) that would be focused on anger management skills, problem-solving ability, techniques for delaying impulsive responses and improve social interactions.
Social – what supports can be put in place for mother? Church, family, structured day care for “respite” time, etc. Consider finding male role models for this child who is the oldest male in his household. Involvement in strength based activities.

Discuss the typical expectations of psychotherapy, including
1. things get worse before they get better – extinction burst
2. behavior therapy requires active participation of the parent and frequent adjustments to rewards
3. typical duration depends on severity of symptoms, adherence to recommendations, etc
4. behavioral training therapy is considered a brief therapy (12-16 sessions)
MK:
A very broad differential diagnosis list should be generated at this point. Some diagnoses should include:
1. Oppositional Defiant Disorder / Conduct Disorder (core feature: “bad” behavior)
2. Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder (core feature: persistent irritable mood)
3. Adjustment Disorders (recent bullying, abuse, physical body changes) (core feature: proximal precipitating event)
4. Depressive Disorders (core feature: in kids irritability, also sad mood)
5. Anxiety Disorders (core feature: worry, also somatic complaints)
6. Substance Related and Addictive Disorders (core feature: drug use)
7. Intermittent Explosive Disorder (core feature: normal most of time, explosive outbursts)
8. Specific Learning Disorders (core feature: difficulty in an academic environment)
